introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K. Relative atomic masses: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ag = 108.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The following flow diagram shows the various stages in the manufacture of nitric acid.

$$
\mathrm{N_2 + H_2} \;\xrightarrow{\;\mathbf{A}\;}\; \mathrm{NH_3} \;\xrightarrow[\;X\;]{\;\mathbf{B}\;}\; \text{Nitrogen monoxide} \;\xrightarrow{\;\mathbf{C}\;}\; \text{Nitrogen dioxide} \longrightarrow \text{Nitric acid}
$$
incertitudes: Points imprimes 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10, conformes au total. Le schema d'ecoulement imprime est recopie sous forme d'equation fleche (A, B, C sur les fleches, X sous la fleche B). Coquille du sujet « Nitrogen droxide » lue « Nitrogen dioxide ».

2(a) : le sujet ne dit pas que A est le procede Haber ; le catalyseur attendu (fer) est celui du programme usuel, le sujet n'imprime pas de corrige. 2(b)(i) : X = oxygene deduit du produit du stage B (NO).

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the catalyst used in stage A. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Stage A is the Haber process, $\mathrm{N_2 + 3H_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3}$. The catalyst is **iron** (finely divided).

questions.enonce_markdown:
At stage B another substance X is added.

(i) Identify the substance X.

(ii) Write a balanced equation for the reaction at stage B. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **X is oxygen** (supplied as air).

(ii) Ammonia is oxidised to nitrogen monoxide over a hot platinum-rhodium catalyst (about 900 $^\circ$C):

$4\mathrm{NH_3} + 5\mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{NO} + 6\mathrm{H_2O}$

Check: N 4 = 4; H 12 = 12; O 10 = 4 + 6.

questions.enonce_markdown: How is the nitrogen monoxide converted to nitrogen dioxide? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The gas is cooled and **mixed with more oxygen (air)**; nitrogen monoxide combines with oxygen at once: $2\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NO_2}$ (colourless gas turning brown).

questions.enonce_markdown: How is the nitrogen dioxide finally converted to nitric acid? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Nitrogen dioxide is **dissolved in water in the presence of excess oxygen (air)**:

$4\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{O_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{HNO_3}$

Check: N 4 = 4; H 4 = 4; O 8 + 2 + 2 = 12 = 4 x 3.

questions.enonce_markdown: The nitric acid prepared in the laboratory is coloured. State the colour. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: It is **yellow** (yellowish-brown), because it contains dissolved nitrogen dioxide formed by the decomposition of the acid.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give two large scale uses of nitric acid. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Any two of: manufacture of **fertilisers** (ammonium nitrate); manufacture of **explosives** (TNT, nitroglycerine); manufacture of dyes; manufacture of plastics and nylon.
